title: Off-diagonal Rado number for $x+y+c=z$ and $x+qy=z$
summary: Ramsey-type problems for linear equations began with Schur's theorem and were systematically generalized by Richard Rado. In the off-diagonal framework for two colors, one considers two different linear equations $(\mathcal{E}_1,\mathcal{E}_2)$ and determines the minimum integer $N$ for which any red-blue coloring of $\{1,2,...,N\}$ forces either a red solution of the equation $\mathcal{E}_1$ or a blue solution of the equation $\mathcal{E}_2$.
